# Epilogue: Holy Ruler

“We return this land to order and prosperity, we bring to it a balanced rule, a stewardship until such time that we are able to return a ruler who is worthy of your obedience, we return the nobility to their lands and bring back the rules and dictates of the Emperor, the true ruler of this land. We the Messengers of Aurtus will ensure continuity until a new Emperor or Empress is found.” The Lord Regent announced to the gathered people of Vicor, the entire commons were packed with nobles and common alike as a cheer rose up to greet his words. The Lord Regent spoke from the balcony of the palace where the church now ruled.

Nero had returned prosperity, freed the children and shutdown the tower. Things were beginning to look like they would come back to normal Marcus thought leaning in the doorway and watching the speech.

Soldiers walked by eyeing his clothing; the outlook towards mages had not improved, but at the same time the church had not spoken of the agreement or their ultimate intentions. Marcus hoped for the best as he turned back toward the room where his friends sat. Corliss, now the Lord Adjudicator of the new Wardens, stood resplendent in her new leather armor complete with the crest of the wardens emblazoned upon it; Uri had retired to live in peace with the Silvans; Dara, Maelen, and Patrice sat around the small table listening as the Regent continued to speak of prosperity and peace.

“So, what’s next?” Maelen asked looking towards Marcus who shifted uncomfortably his friend had seen the packed bag by the door and knew what that meant. “I am heading north. There is a lot to see, and this place holds too many bad memories for now,” he said, seeing Dara’s face fall.

“You’re leaving?” she asked, stepping close to him. Marcus took the young mage gently by the shoulders.

“There is something out there, something I can’t explain. The Empress said things to me that lead me to believe she saw it too,” he said quietly. “I am going to find out what I can. I will be back, but there is much that I need to discover.”

The speech ended to applause and Marcus nodded to his friends. Corliss came over first “Look me up when you come back, Marcus. A lot of what’s going on today is because of you. For that, you have my thanks,” she said, giving him a warm hug before stepping back. Maelen walked him out “Where will you go, back to the Silvan’s?” he asked walking with his friend as he left the small house and headed towards the stables. Marcus was quiet for a few minutes and then looked at his friend “Not sure, I think I am going to find out what else is out there, Durass spoke of other people further north, I want to see if they might know something about these dreams” he said. His friend was quiet for a long time. “When you come back, we should have the order back, if the new ruler allows it” he said wincing, knowing how Nero felt about the mages.

“Take care, my friend. I will see you when I get back,” Marcus said, embracing Maelen. He turned and strode past the courtyard to where the great white cat waited outside the stables—the stable boys refusing to go anywhere near the beast.

Mounting the cat, he rode out through the northern gates of the capital. Reaching the crest of the ridge, Marcus looked back one last time at the city, bowed his head, and whispered a quiet prayer for his friends. Then, with a gentle touch against the beast’s flanks, he turned northward, riding into the gathering dusk.
